newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks reach record highs for second day.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks reach record highs for second day.

text.p: Caracas stocks reached record highs Tuesday for the second consecutive session as investors displayed growing confidence in Venezuela's privatization program, traders said.

"It's been a very good signal that the Banco de Venezuela sale is going ahead," said Interacciones broker Freddy Zambrano. He said foreign bids had focused on food producer Mavesa and bellwether Electricidad de Caracas.
The bolsa's 19-share .IBC index rose 1.99 percent to close at 4,712.76 points, according to preliminary figures.
Among issues that were traded, 29 stocks rose, six fell and seven were unchanged on volume of 16 million shares worth 2.45 billion bolivars ($5.2 million).

Investor confidence has improved because of "falling country risk, rising oil revenues and an accelerating privatization program, whose proceeds will be used to pay off foreign debt," said Merinvest analyst Boris Molina.

Among the day's gainers, Mavesa climbed 7.00 bolivars to close at 129.00 bolivars, Electricidad rose 10.55 bolivars to 401.55, while Sivensa's Class B ADR recouped some of Monday's losses by adding 50.00 bolivars to end at 1,425.00
"Foreign investor interest has remained pretty constant in the bolsa's leading shares," Molina said.
